question: Did training-time linear reparameterization reach a better optimum than the ordinary network, and can it ship?

registeredResult.metric: per-clip mean dB vs frozen production, clip-first
registeredResult.interpretation: The registered test cannot return below 0.100 at three seeds per arm, so it neither establishes nor refutes the effect. R3 won the ladder by the registered rule, which is a selection, not a significance claim.

postHocSupport.status: NOT REGISTERED; computed after the binding result and reported as description only
postHocSupport.perCrfOrdering: R3 leads R1, R2 and R0 at CRF 18, 26 and 34 alike
postHocSupport.whatThisDoesAndDoesNotShow: It shows the advantage is spread across the corpus rather than carried by one or two clips. It does not replace the seed-level test: it conditions on the three seeds actually trained and therefore cannot separate a real parameterization effect from a lucky seed draw. Treating it as the headline would be choosing the test after seeing the data.

whyNothingShips.cause: Measured: every arm trained 16,200 optimizer updates, the shipped model trained 81,180, and all four rungs land about 0.14 dB below it. Not measured: any arm at the production budget. The budget asymmetry is therefore a confound large enough to explain the gap, not a demonstrated cause of it. An architecture explanation has not been excluded by measurement; the design simply made it untestable here.
whyNothingShips.preRegistrationFlaw: A defect in my own pre-registration. Holding the step budget constant is correct for comparing rungs against each other, but setting the replacement gate against a model trained five times longer made the two halves of the protocol incommensurable. The nearest arm missed the +0.10 dB threshold by 0.23 dB, so no candidate came close; "could never have passed" would be a claim about runs nobody made and is not asserted. Recorded as a flaw rather than reinterpreted after the fact.

deployedCost.runtime: results/m7-runtime-parity.json: candidate p50 6.02 and 6.63 ms against production 6.09 and 6.31 ms, difference below run-to-run spread
deployedCost.note: The zero-cost property holds: R3 deploys the identical graph at indistinguishable runtime.

conclusion: Structural reparameterization did not fail. R3 is the best rung by the registered rule and its advantage is broad across the corpus, but at three seeds the registered test cannot establish it, and no candidate met the replacement criterion. Whether R3 still leads at the production budget is unmeasured and is the open question.
correctsEarlierClaim: Earlier wording in results/m7-corrected-screen-plan.json and in commit messages b54a4e2 and ecda18e asserted that budget caused the gap and that a screening-budget seed could not reach the threshold. Those commits stand as history; this record is the correction. Both statements went beyond the evidence, because no matched-budget arm was ever trained.
